result.title: SPARCL: Spatially Adaptive Regional Coverage for Active Learning in Chest X-ray Analysis
result.summary: Pixel-level annotation for chest X-ray (CXR) lesion segmentation is expensive, making active learning (AL) essential. However, existing AL strategies fail to account for the spatial distribution of selected samples, resulting in inconsistent performance across focal (e.g., aortic calcification) and diffuse (e.g., nodules) pathologies. In this paper, we propose SPARCL (Spatially Adaptive Regional Coverage for Active Learning) to dynamically balance predictive uncertainty with cumulative spatial coverage. By employing a concave coverage function, SPARCL imposes diminishing returns on previously annotated regions, naturally directing the annotation budget toward under-labeled areas. Furthermore, an entropy gate reverts the algorithm to standard uncertainty sampling when spatial variation is absent. This coverage objective is monotone submodular, guaranteeing near-optimal greedy batch selection. To address how aggregate metrics like Dice obscure regional failures, we further introduce two metrics---Spatial Inconsistency (SI) and Performance Coverage (PC)---to quantify anatomical fairness across AL rounds. Evaluated on an in-house calcification cohort and public CXR benchmarks, SPARCL reaches 95% of fully supervised performance using only 24% of the data, compared to 29% for the best baseline. Ultimately, SPARCL ensures robust spatial reliability, surfacing regional gains that aggregate metrics miss.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPARCL：面向胸片病灶分割的主动学习策略，用凹形覆盖函数对已标注区域施加递减收益以平衡预测不确定性与空间覆盖，并以熵门在无空间变化时退回标准不确定性采样，另提出 SI 与 PC 两个区域级指标衡量各轮解剖公平性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「覆盖优先」证据采集与次模贪心选择可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/证据筛选提供线索，SI、PC 这类区域级而非聚合指标也可供核查用于评估 latent 视觉信息的实际使用，但属远域迁移推测。
